findings.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — Unauthenticated GET /embed/best with a forged `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and a fresh `embed_url` per request enqueues an unbounded number of RetrieveTopic jobs and forces real topic/post creation as `embed_by_username`; the per-URL redis throttle is bypassed for free because every distinct URL gets its own key.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — A single unauthenticated embed request for an unknown URL synchronously runs the whole hourly feed importer via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside the RetrieveTopic worker, so requests can force repeated full-feed re-imports and a slow/hanging feed host (open-uri sets no timeout) blocks Sidekiq workers and stalls every unrelated job on the queue.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Running PollFeed inline inside RetrieveTopic silently defeats its `sidekiq_options retry: false`: a raising feed item now makes the retrying RetrieveTopic job re-open the feed URL and re-import/re-revise every item up to 25 times with backoff.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote` fetches with `open(url)`, which follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, so `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the first hop; an open redirect on the embeddable host turns the fetcher into an SSRF proxy whose response body is stored as a raw_html post and served publicly.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — post.present?` is true for the unsaved Post that PostCreator returns after `raise ActiveRecord::Rollback` (swallowed without rolling back because `Post.transaction` joins the outer `Topic.transaction`), so a host-spam-flagged imported article reaches `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil)` and dies on the NOT NULL constraint instead of being skipped.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" pass only because `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false and short-circuits the guard; deleting either condition from `execute` leaves both examples green.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:14 — Every example stubs `poll_feed`, the method that does all the work, so no spec ever executes SimpleRSS parsing, `i.content.scrub`, or `TopicEmbed.import` — the entire feed feature can be non-functional with a fully green suite.

spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33 — Every example stubs `perform_retrieve` (the method under test) or `retrieved_recently?`, so gutting the redis throttle, the existence check, the inline PollFeed call, and `fetch_http` would not fail a single spec.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for a standard RSS 2.0 item that has only `description` (no content:encoded), and with `retry: false` the exception aborts the whole run, so every item after the first such entry is silently never imported, every hour, forever.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — post = embed.post` is nil once an imported post is deleted (no FK, no dependent option, no nil guard), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises and permanently kills the rest of the non-retrying hourly feed run; the stale TopicEmbed row also makes `perform_retrieve` bail out forever so the article can never be re-imported.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is varchar(255) with no truncation or validation, so an attacker-padded query string on a real article URL makes `TopicEmbed.create!` fail only after PostCreator created the topic/post and enqueued post-processing jobs pre-commit — 25 Sidekiq retries each burn a create-and-rollback and leave orphan jobs pointing at vanished post ids.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s with no attempt cap or give-up state, so any URL that can never import (blank `embed_by_username`, Readability failure, PostCreator rejection) turns every open iframe into a permanent loop of embed requests, Sidekiq jobs, and outbound fetches of the third-party article.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 — fetch_http` silently `return`s when `embed_by_username` is unset or wrong, so a half-configured site is indistinguishable from "still loading" — the iframe reloads every 30s forever and no error is ever surfaced or logged.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The feed-supplied URL is interpolated unescaped into the "Imported from" anchor and the result is stored verbatim as `cooked` via raw_html, so a feed `<link>` such as `http://x' onmouseover='...` injects attacker-controlled HTML attributes into every reader's page; the Readability tag whitelist never touches this appended string and the PollFeed path never sanitizes at all.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The retriever example asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` with no `.with(...)`, so the security-relevant `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` argument and the embed_url actually forwarded are entirely unverified; the controller in fact calls `Jobs.enqueue`, which no spec checks.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48 — TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, leaving `@topic_view` nil, and controller specs do not render views, so the `after` hook's `response.should be_success` stays green even though `best.html.erb` would raise on `@topic_view.posts` in a real request — the rendered success path has zero coverage.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` and `expire` are not atomic: a worker kill or redis error between the two leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL, permanently throttling that article with no way to distinguish the poisoned key from "still loading".

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is `Kernel#open`, so a feed URL beginning with `|` executes a shell command; the setting has no format validation and this code path is reachable from an unauthenticated embed request through TopicRetriever.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — absolutize_urls` calls `URI(url)` with no rescue (unlike `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), so one feed item whose link contains a space or other invalid character raises InvalidURIError and aborts the entire non-retrying hourly import.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to the transient "loading" response as well as the rendered one, so proxies and CDNs cache "Loading Discussion..." for 60s and the 30s JS reload races the cache — the topic can exist while every visitor keeps getting the loading page.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:10 — All three negative examples assert only `response.should_not be_success`, which passes for any exception at all, so an unrelated 500 is indistinguishable from the referer/host gate actually rejecting the request.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` is a check-then-act with no lock, so two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL (staff `no_throttle`, or after the 60s key expires) both create a topic; the loser's unique-index violation rolls back the topic but the jobs PostCreator enqueued pre-commit still reference the vanished post.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — import_remote` performs the outbound `open(url)` fetch before `import` applies the `^https?://` scheme check, so URL validation happens strictly after the request has already been made.

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` parses as a modifier `if` that swallows the next generated buffer statement as its condition (truthy today, so it renders); it is a hard SyntaxError under stdlib ERB/Erubi and no spec renders this template, so the breakage would ship green.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The postMessage guard is a substring test (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)`) rather than an equality check, and `e.data.height` is unbounded, so any frame on the embedding page whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl can resize the Discourse iframe to arbitrary height.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — Unauthenticated GET /embed/best with a forged `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and a fresh `embed_url` per request enqueues an unbounded number of RetrieveTopic jobs and forces real topic/post creation as `embed_by_username`; the per-URL redis throttle is bypassed for free because every distinct URL gets its own key.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, with no deduplication or rate limiting at the controller layer. The only gating is `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; a non-browser client can forge `Referer` and pass this check. In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, throttling is per-URL using the Redis key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`. An attacker can supply a fresh `embed_url` each time (still under the allowed host) to avoid the throttle and cause unbounded job enqueueing and repeated remote fetch attempts. If `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is configured (required for actual import), `fetch_http` will call `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which can create new topics/posts as that user for each distinct URL, making the amplification concrete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — A single unauthenticated embed request for an unknown URL synchronously runs the whole hourly feed importer via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside the RetrieveTopic worker, so requests can force repeated full-feed re-imports and a slow/hanging feed host (open-uri sets no timeout) blocks Sidekiq workers and stalls every unrelated job on the queue.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Running PollFeed inline inside RetrieveTopic silently defeats its `sidekiq_options retry: false`: a raising feed item now makes the retrying RetrieveTopic job re-open the feed URL and re-import/re-revise every item up to 25 times with backoff.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` (`perform_retrieve`) it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline instead of enqueuing the scheduled job. That means `Jobs::PollFeed`’s `sidekiq_options retry: false` is not honored for this execution path. If `poll_feed` raises (e.g., `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, or an exception during `TopicEmbed.import` for an item), the exception bubbles up through `TopicRetriever#retrieve` into the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), which has no `sidekiq_options retry: false` and will therefore use Sidekiq’s default retry behavior (typically 25 retries with backoff). Each retry would re-run the feed polling and re-process items again until the failure point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote` fetches with `open(url)`, which follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, so `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the first hop; an open redirect on the embeddable host turns the fetcher into an SSRF proxy whose response body is stored as a raw_html post and served publicly.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but `TopicEmbed.import_remote` then does `open(url).read` (open-uri). Open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default, including redirects to a different host. So an attacker-controlled/open-redirect endpoint on the allowed `embeddable_host` could redirect the fetch to an arbitrary internal/external host (SSRF), and the fetched body is then processed and ultimately imported/stored as a `raw_html` post (`cook_method: :raw_html`), making the SSRF response persist and be served later. This is a concrete, verifiable security issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — post.present?` is true for the unsaved Post that PostCreator returns after `raise ActiveRecord::Rollback` (swallowed without rolling back because `Post.transaction` joins the outer `Topic.transaction`), so a host-spam-flagged imported article reaches `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil)` and dies on the NOT NULL constraint instead of being skipped.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" pass only because `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false and short-circuits the guard; deleting either condition from `execute` leaves both examples green.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the examples "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub the one setting under test (to nil) and do not stub SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml is feed_polling_enabled: false, execute will short-circuit on the first condition and never call poll_feed regardless of the other two checks. Therefore, removing either the feed_polling_url or embed_by_username guard from execute would not cause these examples to fail, meaning the tests do not actually verify those guards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:14 — Every example stubs `poll_feed`, the method that does all the work, so no spec ever executes SimpleRSS parsing, `i.content.scrub`, or `TopicEmbed.import` — the entire feed feature can be non-functional with a fully green suite.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, every example sets an expectation on `poll_feed` (`expects(:poll_feed).never/once`), which in Mocha both asserts and stubs the method. As a result, the implementation of `poll_feed` (SimpleRSS.parse/open, `i.content.scrub`, and `TopicEmbed.import`) is never executed by these specs; they only test the gating logic in `execute`. The claim that the "entire feed feature can be non-functional with a fully green suite" is somewhat overstated because other specs could exist elsewhere, but the lack of any test coverage for the core `poll_feed` behavior is real and verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33 — Every example stubs `perform_retrieve` (the method under test) or `retrieved_recently?`, so gutting the redis throttle, the existence check, the inline PollFeed call, and `fetch_http` would not fail a single spec.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` never exercises the real implementations of `perform_retrieve` or `retrieved_recently?`. In all examples it sets Mocha expectations on `perform_retrieve` (replacing the method body) and, in the “valid host” context, stubs `retrieved_recently?` to `true/false`. As a result, the spec does not cover the Redis throttle logic in `retrieved_recently?` nor the `perform_retrieve` internals (embed existence check, optional inline `Jobs::PollFeed` execution, or `fetch_http`). Removing/emptying those implementations would still leave these specs passing, so the finding about ineffective coverage is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for a standard RSS 2.0 item that has only `description` (no content:encoded), and with `retry: false` the exception aborts the whole run, so every item after the first such entry is silently never imported, every hour, forever.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content.scrub` can raise NoMethodError when RSS items lack `content` (only have `description`), which is the same nil/absent content issue described in the golden comment. It also adds additional impact details (run aborts), but the core bug matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — post = embed.post` is nil once an imported post is deleted (no FK, no dependent option, no nil guard), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises and permanently kills the rest of the non-retrying hourly feed run; the stale TopicEmbed row also makes `perform_retrieve` bail out forever so the article can never be re-imported.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` row is found, it does `post = embed.post` and then (if `content_sha1` changed) unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` (lines around the proposed location). If the associated Post was deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil` (there is no FK constraint in the migration and no `dependent:` cleanup shown), so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise and abort the feed job (`Jobs::PollFeed` has no rescue and `sidekiq_options retry: false`). Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` immediately returns if any `TopicEmbed` exists for the URL, so an orphaned/stale `TopicEmbed` row will prevent future re-import attempts for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is varchar(255) with no truncation or validation, so an attacker-padded query string on a real article URL makes `TopicEmbed.create!` fail only after PostCreator created the topic/post and enqueued post-processing jobs pre-commit — 25 Sidekiq retries each burn a create-and-rollback and leave orphan jobs pointing at vanished post ids.

adjudication.rationale: The migration does create `embed_url` as a Rails `string` (typically VARCHAR(255)) and the model only validates presence, so overly long URLs could indeed cause a DB-level error on insert/update depending on the DB/SQL mode. However, the finding’s core claim (PostCreator successfully creates the topic/post, enqueues post-processing jobs “pre-commit”, then `TopicEmbed.create!` fails leaving orphaned jobs pointing at rolled-back post IDs with “25 Sidekiq retries”) is not verifiable from this diff. The `TopicEmbed.create!` happens inside a `Topic.transaction`, which would roll back the created post/topic on exception, and nothing in the diff shows Sidekiq jobs being enqueued before commit or any specific retry count behavior tied to this failure. That part is speculative beyond the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s with no attempt cap or give-up state, so any URL that can never import (blank `embed_by_username`, Readability failure, PostCreator rejection) turns every open iframe into a permanent loop of embed requests, Sidekiq jobs, and outbound fetches of the third-party article.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The new `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads the iframe every 30 seconds (`document.location.reload()`), with no cap/backoff or terminal state. If the embed can never be created (e.g., settings misconfigured or import failing), each reload triggers another request to `/embed/best` and another `retrieve_topic` enqueue. While `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the *fetch* to once per 60s per URL, it does not prevent repeated controller enqueues and repeated iframe reload requests, so the “permanent loop” and Sidekiq job churn are real consequences of the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 — fetch_http` silently `return`s when `embed_by_username` is unset or wrong, so a half-configured site is indistinguishable from "still loading" — the iframe reloads every 30s forever and no error is ever surfaced or logged.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, it looks up `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?`. There is no check in `EmbedController#best`/`ensure_embeddable` that `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is set, so an admin can configure `embeddable_host` correctly (allowing the iframe route to work) but leave `embed_by_username` blank or incorrect. In that case, the background job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) will run and `fetch_http` will simply return without creating a `TopicEmbed`, while the controller continues to render `loading` and the client-side template reloads every 30s (`loading.html.erb`) indefinitely, with no surfaced error. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The feed-supplied URL is interpolated unescaped into the "Imported from" anchor and the result is stored verbatim as `cooked` via raw_html, so a feed `<link>` such as `http://x' onmouseover='...` injects attacker-controlled HTML attributes into every reader's page; the Readability tag whitelist never touches this appended string and the PollFeed path never sanitizes at all.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `url` is only checked with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, then interpolated directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"` which is inserted into `contents`. Because the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore a feed-supplied `link` like `http://x' onmouseover='...` would break out of the quoted `href` attribute and inject attacker-controlled attributes/HTML into the stored content. The Readability whitelist in `import_remote` applies to `doc.content` only and does not sanitize the appended “Imported from” anchor, and the `PollFeed` path also feeds unsanitized content into `TopicEmbed.import`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The retriever example asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` with no `.with(...)`, so the security-relevant `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` argument and the embed_url actually forwarded are entirely unverified; the controller in fact calls `Jobs.enqueue`, which no spec checks.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues a background job when no embed exists: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` contains an example that expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` to be called. That expectation is not just missing `.with(...)`; it contradicts the actual controller implementation and will fail (and it also means the spec never asserts that `Jobs.enqueue` is called with the correct `embed_url`/`user_id`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48 — TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, leaving `@topic_view` nil, and controller specs do not render views, so the `after` hook's `response.should be_success` stays green even though `best.html.erb` would raise on `@topic_view.posts` in a real request — the rendered success path has zero coverage.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` and `expire` are not atomic: a worker kill or redis error between the two leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL, permanently throttling that article with no way to distinguish the poisoned key from "still loading".

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are not atomic. If the worker dies, crashes, or a Redis/network error occurs after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key `retrieved:<embed_url>` can be left without a TTL. Because subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (throttled), that URL can be permanently treated as “retrieved recently” until the key is manually deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is `Kernel#open`, so a feed URL beginning with `|` executes a shell command; the setting has no format validation and this code path is reachable from an unauthenticated embed request through TopicRetriever.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — absolutize_urls` calls `URI(url)` with no rescue (unlike `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), so one feed item whose link contains a space or other invalid character raises InvalidURIError and aborts the entire non-retrying hourly import.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` does `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue. The only guard before calling it is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not ensure the URL is a valid RFC URI (e.g., spaces or other invalid characters can still match). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` inside `rss.items.each` with no exception handling, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so an `URI::InvalidURIError` from one bad feed item would abort the whole hourly import run and it would not be retried by Sidekiq.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to the transient "loading" response as well as the rendered one, so proxies and CDNs cache "Loading Discussion..." for 60s and the 30s JS reload races the cache — the topic can exist while every visitor keeps getting the loading page.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called unconditionally after the `if topic_id ... else ... render 'loading' end` block. In Rails, `render 'loading'` does not automatically stop execution of the action, so the cache headers set by `discourse_expires_in` will also apply to the loading response. That makes it possible for intermediaries (or even the browser) to cache the "Loading Discussion..." page for up to 60 seconds, so the 30s JS `document.location.reload()` can repeatedly hit the cached loading response even after the topic has been created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:10 — All three negative examples assert only `response.should_not be_success`, which passes for any exception at all, so an unrelated 500 is indistinguishable from the referer/host gate actually rejecting the request.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the three “negative” cases (`get :best` without embed_url, missing embeddable_host, and no referer) only assert `response.should_not be_success`. That expectation will pass for any non-2xx response, including an unrelated 500 caused by an exception, and does not verify the intended failure mode (e.g., specific status code, raised error type/message). This makes the tests unable to distinguish correct gate rejection from unrelated controller breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` is a check-then-act with no lock, so two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL (staff `no_throttle`, or after the 60s key expires) both create a topic; the loser's unique-index violation rolls back the topic but the jobs PostCreator enqueued pre-commit still reference the vanished post.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a classic check-then-act race in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`: it does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which may create a new `TopicEmbed` row (unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` is added in the migration). Two concurrent `RetrieveTopic` executions for the same URL can both pass the `exists?` check and then both attempt to create; the “loser” will hit a unique constraint violation at `TopicEmbed.create!` inside `TopicEmbed.import` and raise, failing the job. However, the finding’s claim about “PostCreator enqueued pre-commit still reference the vanished post” is not verifiable from this diff (no such enqueueing is shown), and the transaction in `TopicEmbed.import` would roll back the post/topic as well. So the race/unique-violation failure is real, but the described downstream effect is partly speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — import_remote` performs the outbound `open(url)` fetch before `import` applies the `^https?://` scheme check, so URL validation happens strictly after the request has already been made.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` immediately when building the `Readability::Document`:

```rb
doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)
TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)
```

The `^https?://` validation is only performed inside `TopicEmbed.import`:

```rb
return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//
```

So for any non-HTTP(S) URL (or otherwise malformed URL that `open` will still try to handle), the outbound/local fetch attempt happens before the scheme check can block it. This makes the finding accurate and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` parses as a modifier `if` that swallows the next generated buffer statement as its condition (truthy today, so it renders); it is a hard SyntaxError under stdlib ERB/Erubi and no spec renders this template, so the breakage would ship green.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The postMessage guard is a substring test (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)`) rather than an equality check, and `e.data.height` is unbounded, so any frame on the embedding page whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl can resize the Discourse iframe to arbitrary height.

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — An already-released migration is retroactively edited to add `force: true`, which silently drops and recreates `top_topics` (losing data) on any environment where that migration is re-run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. That is a behavior change that can cause silent data loss if this migration is ever executed against a database where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., a re-run/partial migrate scenario). The risk is directly implied by the code change, even though whether it is "already released" cannot be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is the raw unescaped request.referer (full URL with path/query), which breaks the resize protocol and allows JS string injection via a crafted Referer
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both point out that postMessage is using request.referer as targetOrigin (a full URL including path/query) instead of just the origin (scheme+host+port), which causes postMessage to drop the message and breaks the resize behavior. The candidate additionally mentions injection risk, but the core issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Host-page origin check uses substring match (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of exact origin comparison, so unrelated origins can drive the discourse-resize protocol
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the origin validation is flawed because it relies on a substring check using indexOf rather than an exact origin match, allowing malicious/unrelated domains (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com) to pass the check and interact with the protocol.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — raw_html cook path returns raw and bypasses the Plugin::Filter(:after_post_cook) contract, so every consumer of `cooked` (serializers, RSS, email) receives unfiltered third-party HTML

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). This bypasses the normal cooking pipeline `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and also bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, meaning no post-processing/sanitization/hooks run for these posts. The diff also introduces a path that sets this cook_method for imported third-party HTML (`TopicEmbed.import` uses `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...[:raw_html])`, where `contents` comes from RSS/readability). As a result, consumers of `post.cooked` will receive the raw imported HTML without the usual filtering/hooking, which is a real behavioral/security risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — Response depends on Referer (access check + X-Frame-Options) and current_user but is marked cacheable for 1 minute with no Vary, so shared caches can leak the embed HTML across hosts/users

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, access control is enforced in ensure_embeddable by checking `URI(request.referer).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and it also sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL` only after that check. However, the action unconditionally calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` at the end, making the response cacheable. If `discourse_expires_in` results in a shared-cacheable response (as its name implies), a reverse proxy/CDN could cache the HTML for a given `GET /embed/best?embed_url=...` and later serve it to requests that would otherwise fail the referer/host check, since the app would not be hit. Additionally, the rendered content can vary with `current_user` (passed into `TopicView.new` / `Jobs.enqueue` user_id), but no `Vary` or other cache partitioning by user/referer is present in the diff. This is a real cache-leak/bypass risk introduced by combining referer-based authorization with cacheable responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — Embed snippet requires an undocumented trailing slash on discourseUrl and an existing #discourse-comments element, with no normalization or guard for embedders

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe URL is built via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. This will produce an invalid URL if `discourseUrl` does not end with `/` (e.g. `https://forum.example.comembed/best`). The code also does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and immediately calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no null-check, so if the host page lacks that element it will throw a runtime error. Both issues are directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — Missing embed_url raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, giving embedders a 500 instead of a 4xx contract response

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the line `params.require(:embed_url)` will indeed raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when `embed_url` is absent. However, in Rails 4 (as implied by `Gemfile_rails4.lock`), `ActionController::ParameterMissing` is mapped via Rails' `rescue_responses` to a 400 Bad Request (a 4xx), not an unhandled 500. The diff itself does not show any custom exception handling that would convert this into a 500, so the claim that embedders get a 500 is not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is a non-standard value that some browsers do not honor; the header should be removed for embeddable responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_embeddable` which sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28). `ALLOWALL` is not a standard/recognized X-Frame-Options directive (standard values are typically `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and the obsolete/limited `ALLOW-FROM`), so some user agents may ignore or mishandle it, potentially breaking the intended embedding behavior. The presence of this non-standard header value is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8 — Height is posted only once on window.onload with no re-post on later content/image layout changes and no host-initiated request, so the iframe keeps a stale height

If `revise!` returns `false` (e.g., `should_revise?` fails / post not editable / no revision applied), the stored `content_sha1` will be updated anyway, no longer matching the actual post content and preventing future retries because subsequent imports will see matching hashes and skip the revise path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — SETNX + EXPIRE are not atomic; a crash between them leaves the throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed_url.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — Check-then-insert on embed_url races with concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic runs and violates the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url.

With concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic runs importing the same URL, two workers can both observe no existing row and then both attempt `create!`. The second will hit the unique index `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true` and raise an exception (not rescued), causing the job/request to fail. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding a NOT NULL column with a default to the huge `posts` table forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock (PG < 11), blocking the site during deploy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Editing an already-released migration to add `force: true` is a no-op on existing installs and silently DROPs an existing `top_topics` table (data loss) wherever it does re-run.

Since this is an already-versioned migration, it will not run again on existing installs (so the change is a no-op there), but if the migration is re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, `db:reset`, or in an environment where the table already exists for any reason), it will silently DROP `top_topics` and recreate it, causing data loss for any data in that table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — perform_retrieve runs the entire hourly PollFeed job synchronously (full feed download + import of every item) for each embed URL miss, duplicating the scheduled job's work.

adjudication.rationale:

```rb
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?

end
```

Jobs::PollFeed is defined as a scheduled hourly job (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) that synchronously fetches `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, parses the whole feed, and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item. Calling this from TopicRetriever means every embed miss (i.e., every request/job for a new embed_url) can trigger a full feed download + import pass, duplicating the scheduled polling work and potentially doing that many times (especially across different embed URLs, since the throttle key is per-embed_url). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open() on the feed URL has no timeout, redirect or size limit, so a slow/huge remote feed blocks the worker (and the inline TopicRetriever path) indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `open-uri` without specifying any network safeguards (e.g., open_timeout/read_timeout, max redirects, max response size). Because it reads and parses the entire remote response, a feed endpoint that is very slow, streams data continuously, or returns an extremely large body can tie up the Sidekiq worker for an unbounded amount of time/memory. This same call path can be triggered inline from `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true (it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), so the lack of limits affects both the scheduled job and the on-demand retrieval path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key computes a cache key that is never used, so there is no conditional GET/If-Modified-Since and the whole feed is refetched and every item re-hashed and re-queried each run.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a method `feed_key` is defined (building a Redis-style key based on the feed URL), but it is never referenced anywhere in the job. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key` or any stored last-modified/etag value, so each scheduled run will refetch the full feed and iterate all items, invoking `TopicEmbed.import` for each item again (which recomputes a SHA1 and queries/updates per item). The unused `feed_key` is a verifiable dead-code/unfinished-caching issue in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote does open(url).read, materializing the entire remote page in memory with no timeout or size cap before Readability parses it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote, the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full string to `Readability::Document.new(...)`. This unconditionally reads the entire remote response into memory and uses open-uri defaults (no explicit open/read timeouts, no maximum size), which can lead to excessive memory usage or hanging on slow/large responses. The diff shows no safeguards or limits around this call, so the finding is directly verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — A RetrieveTopic job is enqueued on every cache-missing request with no dedupe before enqueue (throttle is only checked inside the job), so a popular embedding page floods Sidekiq with redundant jobs.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, it unconditionally calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders 'loading'. There is no check before enqueue to see if a retrieve job is already queued/in-flight for that embed_url. The only throttling/deduping shown is in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (Redis SETNX) which runs inside the job (RetrieveTopic#execute -> TopicRetriever#retrieve). So a popular embed page that hasn’t been imported yet can enqueue many redundant RetrieveTopic jobs before the first one completes, even though most will no-op later due to the throttle/exists? checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — The 1-minute cache directive is also applied to the 'loading' placeholder whose script reloads every 30s, so reloads are served stale from caches and lengthen time-to-content.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally at the end of the action, regardless of whether it renders the real embed (`best.html.erb`) or the placeholder (`render 'loading'` when `topic_id` is nil). The `loading.html.erb` view uses `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds. With a 1-minute cache directive applied to the loading response, a reload within that minute can be satisfied from cache (especially since `location.reload()` without `true` may use cached content), causing the client to keep reloading the stale loading page and delaying time-to-content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — post.user is dereferenced per post in the render loop, risking an N+1 user lookup if TopicView's best-posts query does not eager-load users.

adjudication.rationale: The view does dereference `post.user` inside a loop (`post.user.small_avatar_url`, `post.user.username`), which could cause N+1 queries if the posts were not preloaded with users. However, the diff does not show how `TopicView` loads `@topic_view.posts` for the `best` option, nor whether it eager-loads `:user`. Since the alleged N+1 depends on behavior in code not included in the diff, it is not a verifiable problem introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no open/read timeout, so a slow or hanging feed host can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does call `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without explicitly passing `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, so it’s true there are no custom timeouts set in this diff. However, the finding’s claim that this can block a Sidekiq worker “indefinitely” is not verifiable from the diff because Ruby’s `open-uri` uses Net::HTTP defaults (which typically include finite open/read timeouts). At most, this is a hardening suggestion to set explicit timeouts, not a clear defect that will hang forever based solely on the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` in import_remote has no timeout or size limit, so a slow/huge remote page can hang or balloon the RetrieveTopic worker

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) with no `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, or any limit on bytes read. This is directly in the diff (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` call). `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` invoke `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, so a slow server or very large response can block the Sidekiq worker thread and/or consume excessive memory while reading the full body into a string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue in the feed loop: one bad item (nil/invalid content, import failure) aborts the whole poll and skips all remaining items

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code iterates `rss.items.each` and does not rescue exceptions per item. Several operations inside the loop can raise (e.g., `i.content.scrub` will raise if `i.content` is nil, `SimpleRSS.parse` items may have unexpected structure, and `TopicEmbed.import` can raise via `create!` inside a transaction). Any such exception will abort `poll_feed` immediately, preventing remaining feed items from being processed in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Redis throttle uses non-atomic SETNX then EXPIRE; a crash between the two leaves a TTL-less key that permanently blocks retrieval of that embed_url

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic. If the process crashes or the Redis connection drops after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE is applied, the key will remain without a TTL, causing `setnx` to keep returning false and permanently treating that embed_url as "retrieved recently" (blocking future retrieval) until the key is manually deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — RetrieveTopic synchronously runs the entire feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`) inline, so concurrent misses each refetch and reimport the whole feed

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `perform_retrieve` unconditionally does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` fetches and parses the entire feed URL (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates all items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each item—so a single missing `@embed_url` can trigger a full-feed refetch/reimport pass. Since the throttle key is per-embed URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), concurrent requests for different missing embed URLs can each invoke this full feed poll redundantly. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff and represents a real performance/correctness risk (duplicative network work and repeated imports) introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — Check-then-create against the unique embed_url index is racy; concurrent imports raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unrescued and kills the job

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so concurrent imports of the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then one `create!` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue around `create!` here (or in the calling jobs like `Jobs::PollFeed` / `TopicRetriever`), so the exception would bubble up and fail the job/request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` can be nil (post deleted/purged), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole feed poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found, the code does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally uses it in `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the content hash changed. The model does not validate presence of `:post` (only `post_id` column is non-null) and there is no foreign key or dependent constraint shown, so it is possible for `topic_embeds.post_id` to reference a deleted/purged post, making `embed.post` return `nil`. In that case `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will later call methods on `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`) and raise `NoMethodError`, which would abort the feed/embedding import path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — sidekiq_options retry: false` means transient feed/network failures are dropped entirely with no retry before the next hourly run

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `sidekiq_options retry: false` on `Jobs::PollFeed`, so a transient exception during a given run (e.g., `open-uri` network error) will not be retried by Sidekiq. However, this is a common/intentional choice for scheduled polling jobs to avoid building up retry backlogs, and the job is still scheduled to run again hourly (`recurrence { hourly }`). So while the statement is technically accurate about Sidekiq retry behavior, it does not constitute a clear defect introduced by the diff—it's a design tradeoff rather than a verifiable bug/correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — RetrieveTopic is enqueued from the request path on every miss with no dedup, and the loading page auto-reloads every 30s, so crawlers/refreshes can flood the queue

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. There is no deduplication or throttling at enqueue time, so repeated requests for the same `embed_url` will enqueue additional `RetrieveTopic` jobs. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) auto-reloads the page every 30 seconds, which will keep re-enqueuing jobs until the topic is created (or forever if retrieval fails), and crawlers/refreshes can amplify this. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s Redis throttle, that only prevents repeated *work* during job execution; it does not prevent the queue from being filled with redundant jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — Raising InvalidParameters for a permanently malformed arg causes Sidekiq to retry the poison job repeatedly instead of discarding it

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the job raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters` only when `args[:embed_url]` is blank. However, the only enqueue shown in the diff (`EmbedController#best`) uses `params.require(:embed_url)`, so a missing `embed_url` would fail before the job is enqueued. Also, Sidekiq does not “retry repeatedly” forever; it retries a finite number of times and then moves to the dead set (and the diff doesn’t show any custom retry behavior here). So the finding is largely a mischaracterization and not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Remote RSS/Atom item content is CGI.unescapeHTML'd and stored verbatim as a raw_html post with no sanitization, so feed-supplied <script>/on* attributes become stored XSS in the embed view and the normal topic view

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item HTML is taken from `i.content` (or equivalent) and processed only with `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before being passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and because `post.cooked == post.raw` for `raw_html`, any `<script>` tags or `on*` event attributes present in the feed content will be persisted and rendered as executable HTML/JS (stored XSS). The only transformation (`absolutize_urls`) rewrites relative `href/src` but does not sanitize dangerous tags/attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — cook() returns raw unchanged for cook_method raw_html, bypassing the entire sanitization/cook pipeline for imported posts whose HTML comes from untrusted remote pages

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). New RSS/remote import code sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` when creating posts from external content (TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator, app/models/topic_embed.rb). In the scheduled feed importer, `content` is taken from `SimpleRSS` (`i.content.scrub`) and passed into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization step before being stored and later rendered. Because `cook` is bypassed for these posts, any untrusted HTML from feeds (e.g., `<script>`, event handlers, etc.) can be persisted and served as-is, creating an XSS risk (especially since embed views render with `raw post.cooked`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The remote-supplied url is interpolated unescaped into #{url}, so a feed link containing a single quote injects arbitrary attributes/markup (e.g. onmouseover=) into the stored HTML

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code appends an “Imported from” footer by interpolating `url` directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not exclude single quotes or other HTML-breaking characters. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (skipping sanitization), and embed/best.html.erb renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore, a feed-supplied URL containing a single quote can break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/markup into the stored HTML, making this a real XSS/vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — post.cooked is emitted with raw in a page served with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL, rendering unsanitized imported HTML to embedders

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a path where imported content is rendered as raw HTML without sanitization. In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. TopicEmbed.import sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and stores `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from RSS (`i.content`) or Readability (`doc.content`) with no sanitization. Then app/views/embed/best.html.erb emits it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Additionally, the code appends an HTML snippet containing the unescaped `url` inside an `<a href='#{url}'>` (TopicEmbed.import), and the URL validation is only `/^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes in the URL, enabling straightforward attribute-breaking XSS. The embed controller also sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`, making it easier to embed this unsafe HTML. This is a concrete, verifiable security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses Kernel#open, so a feed URL beginning with "|" is executed as a shell command, and no scheme validation is performed on the setting

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` passes an arbitrary string from a site setting directly to `open` with `require 'open-uri'` loaded. Ruby’s `Kernel#open` supports the `open("|cmd")` form (and open-uri extends `open` for URLs), so a setting value beginning with `|` can spawn a subprocess. The code also does not validate that `feed_polling_url` is an `http/https` URL before calling `open`, so non-HTTP schemes or the pipe form aren’t prevented. This is a real, verifiable command-execution/unsafe open risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is built from the attacker-influenced full request.referer URL interpolated into inline JS rather than a validated origin constant

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code does `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');`. The second argument to `postMessage` is `targetOrigin` and must be `'*'` or a valid origin string of the form `scheme://host[:port]`, not a full URL with path/query. `request.referer` is the full Referer URL (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/...`), so this can be an invalid `targetOrigin` (can throw a DOMException in browsers) or at minimum will not match the parent window’s origin, breaking the resize messaging. While the controller validates the Referer host, it does not normalize it to an origin string before embedding it into JS, so the finding correctly identifies a real correctness/security-related issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin validation uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) (substring match) instead of an exact origin comparison and does not verify e.source is the embed iframe

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12 — Every example stubs `poll_feed` itself, so the entire new feed body (SimpleRSS parse/open, link-vs-id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML/scrub, TopicEmbed.import) has zero coverage and no RSS vs Atom shape test.

adjudication.rationale: The new spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only exercises `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`’s guard conditions and uses `poller.expects(:poll_feed)` (Mocha) which replaces/stubs the real `poll_feed` implementation, so the body of `poll_feed` (SimpleRSS.parse/open-uri, item URL fallback, HTML unescape/scrub, `TopicEmbed.import`) is not executed by these tests. However, this is a test coverage critique rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" are tautological: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false in test, so `execute` short-circuits and both pass even if those guards were deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, the guard is `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the examples "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub the respective setting to nil, but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Since the default in config/site_settings.yml is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, `execute` will typically short-circuit on the first condition and never call `poll_feed` regardless of the other two settings. Thus those tests can pass even if the `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` checks were removed, making them effectively tautological / not actually testing the intended guards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — The "valid host" examples stub both `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?` on the object under test, verifying only the two-line boolean wiring in `retrieve`; nothing real is exercised.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` under "with a valid host", both examples stub internal behavior on the object under test: they set expectations on `perform_retrieve` and explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to `true/false`. This means the tests largely verify only that `retrieve` branches based on `retrieved_recently?` (and the host check), without exercising the real throttling/Redis logic or the actual `perform_retrieve` implementation. That is a verifiable weakness in the added spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:22 — The redis throttle (`setnx`/`expire` 60s), its expiry, and the `no_throttle` staff bypass are stubbed out in every example and have no test at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the throttle logic in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx`/`expire 60` behavior and the `no_throttle` bypass) is never exercised: in the “valid host” examples `retrieved_recently?` is explicitly stubbed to `true`/`false`, and the other examples exit early via `invalid_host?`. However, this is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect in the implementation shown in the diff; the diff does not demonstrate the throttle is incorrect, only that it’s untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:39 — perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` (existing-embed bail-out, inline PollFeed re-run, embed_by_username lookup, import_remote) are never executed by any spec.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce specs for TopicRetriever, but they explicitly mock/stub `perform_retrieve` (and `retrieved_recently?`) rather than executing `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` and their internal branches. So it’s true those code paths aren’t covered by these specs. However, that is a test coverage gap, not a verifiable defect/bug/security/correctness problem in the code itself introduced by the diff, and the finding doesn’t point to an actual runtime issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec: the missing-embed_url InvalidParameters raise, the deleted/absent user lookup, and the staff -> no_throttle mapping are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) and does not add a corresponding spec file that exercises its behaviors. However, this is a test coverage/process concern rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The code itself is not shown to be incorrect, only untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — TopicEmbed.import_remote` (the only path used by TopicRetriever and the rewritten disqus.thor) has no test whatsoever, including its nil-title/readability behaviour.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and it is invoked by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the updated `disqus.thor`. However, the proposed finding is about missing test coverage (no spec exercising `.import_remote`/Readability/title behavior). That is verifiable (there are specs for `.import` but none for `.import_remote`), but it is not itself a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code; it’s a testing/coverage suggestion rather than a concrete functional problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The spec asserts `TopicRetriever.new` is called, but the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic; the mock takes no `.with(...)` so embed_url and user_id are never verified and the job layer is skipped.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`, when no `topic_id` is found the controller does **not** instantiate `TopicRetriever`; it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the “tells the topic retriever to work…” example) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, which will never be met given the controller’s implementation. That’s a concrete spec/code mismatch introduced in this diff and would cause the spec to fail. (The note about missing `.with(...)` is secondary; the primary verifiable defect is that the spec asserts the wrong behavior.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48 — TopicView.new` is mocked (returning nil) and controller specs don't render views, so this asserts purely on a stub; the new best/loading/embed layout templates that dereference `@topic_view` get no coverage.
spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:35 — The success context's only assertions live in an `after` hook, so each example body asserts nothing and hook failures are attributed confusingly.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the `context "success"` does place `response.should be_success` and an X-Frame-Options header check in an `after` hook, which could make failures show up as coming from the hook. However, the proposed finding claims "each example body asserts nothing", which is not true in the diff: each `it` block contains concrete expectations (e.g., `TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed)`, `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`, `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, `TopicView.expects(:new)`). This is therefore not a verifiable correctness/security defect introduced by the diff, but at most a test-structure preference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" never reaches `params.require`: blank embeddable_host makes ensure_embeddable reject first, so it duplicates the missing-host case instead of testing the required param.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController, `ensure_embeddable` is a `before_filter` that runs before `best`. It raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. In `site_settings.yml` the default `embeddable_host` is `''` (blank), and the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` does not stub `embeddable_host` or referer. Therefore the request will be rejected by `ensure_embeddable` before the action executes `params.require(:embed_url)`, so the example does not actually test the missing `embed_url` parameter case and effectively overlaps with the missing-host behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — No example covers a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, nor the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch for a malformed Referer header.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable there are two distinct failure paths: (1) referer host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host, and (2) malformed referer causing URI::InvalidURIError, both resulting in InvalidAccess. The added spec (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb) covers missing embed_url, missing embeddable_host, no referer, and a success case with a valid referer, but it does not include any example where the referer is present but from a different host, nor any example where the referer is an invalid URI string to exercise the rescue branch. So the finding about missing test coverage for these branches is verifiably true in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — @post.save` became `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, changing validation behaviour for every revision, with no post_revisor spec added or updated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, but this does not alter validation behavior for every revision—only when the caller explicitly passes `skip_validations: true`.
